title: Ordinary closed module pushforward preserves homology
statement: For schemes Z and Y [def-pc-scheme] and a closed immersion i:Z -> Y [def-weil-closed-immersion], the ordinary module pushforward i_*:Mod(O_Z) -> Mod(O_Y) [def-pc-module-pullback] preserves homology of every short complex: its canonical homology comparison is an isomorphism. This is ordinary O_Y-module pushforward, not pushforward into modules over the direct-image algebra.

source.place: Modules, lemma-closed-immersion-push-pull, exactness assertion; local lifting proof uses the closed embedding and empty-cover sheaf axiom.

proof.text: Use the abelian-sheaf epimorphism/local-surjectivity criterion. For an epimorphism on Z and a section over the inverse image of an ambient open W, lift near a point x of Z. Since i is inducing, the source open on which it lifts is the inverse image of some ambient open V. On V intersect W the restricted lift solves the lifting problem. At a point outside the closed image, the open complement has empty inverse image; target sections are zero by the sheaf axiom, and zero is a lift. This proves preservation of epimorphisms for underlying abelian sheaves in the private helper.

The source-library instance SheafOfModules.preservesFiniteColimits_toSheaf makes forgetting scalars preserve epimorphisms; faithfulness reflects them. Forgetting after ordinary module pushforward is definitionally abelian pushforward after forgetting, so the first step proves preservation of module epimorphisms.
Ordinary module pushforward is a right adjoint, hence preserves kernels. Apply Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels.
